correctness.rationale: Exact finite selected-set/uniform-prefix coupling, maximum and factorial-moment formulas establish the rare variables. Given finitely many forced fixed positions, removing them perturbs descents by at most three times their number, uniformly; combined with the Eulerian CLT, this proves mixed Gaussian/Poisson independence rather than merely separate convergence. Classical full-span bivariate local CLT for Poissonized occupancy provides the occupancy normal law. A finite conditional covariance and boundary identity plus uniform moment bounds and a delta expansion give the unscaled negative covariance. The standalone checker reproduced 1877 deterministic assertions. All proof steps and limits are stated in RESULT.md; finite checks alone are not claimed to certify asymptotic results.

value.rationale: For the natural three statistics of an incomplete random-to-top shuffle, the joint law is not determined by the established marginals. Four-way factorization identifies independent sources of rare and Gaussian uncertainty; the Gaussian descent/occupancy covariance and negative unscaled fixed-point/descent covariance quantify two distinct dependence scales. This directly clarifies simultaneous diagnostics of the same shuffle and is not a synthetic slice, a normalization trick or a finite table update. The independent-audit and complete historical-priority limitations are explicit.
